skill.name: limrun-android-emulator
skill.description: Control Limrun cloud Android emulators to install APKs, test interfaces, collect diagnostics, simulate device conditions, and inspect selected application traffic.
skill.summary: Test and troubleshoot Android applications on Limrun cloud emulators.
skill.author: limrun-inc

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, example URLs, loopback addresses, and commands scoped to a selected emulator. One example can interpolate a package search term inside `sh -c`, creating command-injection risk if untrusted text is substituted. The skill also uploads APKs, shares signed stream links, and can persist decrypted HTTP bodies, so explicit consent and data minimization are required.

remediation.issue: A dynamic package search value appears inside `sh -c`.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the remote shell pipeline, or strictly quote and validate the package search value before substitution.

remediation.issue: Local APKs are uploaded to a third-party cloud service.
remediation.suggestion: Request confirmation before each upload and identify the destination, artifact type, retention policy, and expected project.

remediation.issue: Signed stream URLs may provide bearer-style session access.
remediation.suggestion: Share links only through the active user channel, never place them in public logs, and delete the emulator after use.

remediation.issue: Persistent inspection artifacts include decrypted HTTP bodies.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before inspection or persistence, use synthetic data, minimize selectors and retention, and use `--no-inspect` for sensitive hosts.

content.user_title: Test Android Apps on Cloud Emulators
content.value_statement: Testing Android APKs across remote environments requires device setup, control, and diagnostics. This skill uses Limrun workflows to install, interact, inspect, record, and troubleshoot emulator sessions.
actual_capabilities: Creates or reuses Limrun cloud Android emulator instances with explicit jurisdiction and timeout options.
Installs APKs from local paths, URLs, or uploaded assets and synchronizes changed builds.
Launches and terminates applications while collecting crash details, stack traces, and application logs.
Reads UI element trees and controls applications through selectors, coordinates, typing, scrolling, and key presses.
Captures screenshots and video, injects microphone audio, and simulates limited network bandwidth.
Uses ADB tunnels for shell access, file transfer, logcat, local-service routing, HTTP inspection, and HAR capture.
limitations: Requires the Limrun CLI, valid authentication, network access, and an available cloud emulator account.
Requires an existing APK; application build failures must be handled by a separate build workflow.
Some applications expose no accessibility nodes, requiring less reliable screenshot and coordinate-based interaction.
Certificate-pinned hosts cannot use HTTPS inspection, and persisted traffic artifacts may contain sensitive data.

use_cases.title: Validate a new Android build
use_cases.description: Install an APK, launch the application, exercise changed screens, and confirm expected UI state.

use_cases.title: Reproduce device and network failures
use_cases.description: Collect logs, crash reports, screenshots, and recordings while testing constrained bandwidth or voice input.

use_cases.title: Inspect integration traffic
use_cases.description: Route selected application destinations through a development machine and review authorized HTTP traffic.

prompt_templates.title: Launch an APK
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Limrun Android emulator, install [APK path], launch [package name], and report whether the first screen loads.

prompt_templates.title: Test a user flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Install [APK path], navigate through [flow], verify [expected result] with the element tree, and capture a final screenshot.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose an application failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Launch [package name], reproduce [failure steps], collect the relevant application logs and crash report, then summarize the likely cause.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a controlled integration
prompt_templates.prompt: With my approval, route only [host and port] through the emulator tunnel, reproduce [request], and summarize authorized traffic without persisting sensitive bodies.

output_examples.input: Install the debug APK and verify that the sign-in screen opens.
output_examples.output: The APK installed and launched successfully. The sign-in screen contains email, password, and submit controls, and no crash appeared.

output_examples.input: Reproduce the crash after selecting a saved profile and explain the cause.
output: The crash reproduced after the saved profile was selected.
The application log reports a null value in profile loading.
The failure is isolated to saved profiles missing the required identifier.

output_examples.input: Test the checkout screen under a slow connection and record the result.
output_examples.output: Checkout remained responsive under the approved bandwidth limit. The payment request completed, and the recording shows the loading state and confirmation screen.

best_practices: Confirm the emulator identifier before every action when multiple instances are active.
Use element selectors for assertions and interactions, then use screenshots for visual verification.
Obtain approval before uploads, signed-link sharing, shell access, traffic inspection, or persistent artifacts.
anti_patterns: Do not inspect broad traffic domains when one exact destination is sufficient.
Do not substitute untrusted text into shell commands or reuse commands with unknown arguments.
Do not leave emulators, tunnels, signed links, recordings, or traffic artifacts active after testing.

faq.question: Does this skill build Android applications?
faq.answer: No. It requires a built APK and focuses on installation, interaction, testing, and diagnostics.

faq.question: What authentication is required?
faq.answer: Use an authenticated Limrun CLI session or a configured LIM_API_KEY. Never place the key in prompts or logs.

faq.question: Can it test applications without accessibility nodes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use screenshots and coordinates, but those interactions are less reliable than element selectors.

faq.question: Can it access a local development server?
faq.answer: Yes. A destination tunnel can route an approved host and port through the machine running the Limrun CLI.

faq.question: Does network inspection capture sensitive data?
faq.answer: It can. HTTPS inspection decodes selected traffic, and persistent artifacts can include request and response bodies.

faq.question: What should happen after testing?
faq.answer: Stop tunnels, remove unneeded artifacts, delete the emulator, and avoid retaining signed stream links.
